routines.semantics: Create a temporary EK writer and return an owned opaque handle. EKCLS closes the file and releases scratch storage.

scenarios.observes: A scratch file starts with zero segments and ordinary explicit close releases its claim. Compare the complete independent file workflow, including returned ordinals or persisted effects.
Two scratch writers retain different schema counts when one closes. Compare the complete independent file workflow, including returned ordinals or persisted effects.
The named file and the scratch file can both create segment zero and close independently. Compare the complete independent file workflow, including returned ordinals or persisted effects.
A genuine bad segment on a temporary writer leaves an owned claim for the workflow finalizer. Require INVALIDINDEX.

routines.edgeAssessment: A scratch file starts with zero segments and ordinary explicit close releases its claim. Two scratch writers retain different schema counts when one closes. The named file and the scratch file can both create segment zero and close independently.
routines.errorAssessment: Actual terminal diagnostics include INVALIDINDEX. Adapter ownership, unsupported fixed-count edits, fast-write interruption, allocation failure and ordinal conversion bounds are assessed separately. No incomplete entry is queried.

findings.summary: SpiceyPy character counts do not establish correct byte strides for UTF-8 or an all-empty table.
findings.repair: Use typed independent N0067 rows for those cases and the ordinary locked wrapper for nonempty ASCII arrays. Snapshot validated byte tables for production.

findings.summary: SpiceyPy 6.0.3 transposes the dimensions of cnames in SpiceEKSegSum. Reading its cnames property can hide later column names in multi-column schemas.
findings.repair: Read the same returned 3300-byte field through its verified ctypes offset with canonical 33-byte row stride. Check three different names and every attribute independently.
